items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: Benny Bailey said, "Could I play one?" I said, "Yeah, man, come on."

ctx.x: Well, probably, but see, I couldn't have heard them because I was working too much here. But now Benny Bailey, now, I just come from the Casino de Paris, and they were sitting down there, Benny Bailey was sitting down there just as unconcerned. I always tried somebody to get me, see. They were mad because I was there so long. See, people get mad, 'What is he doing down there?' Kenny say, well, whatever he's doing down there, he's down there, so let him alone. Kenny's at the Blue Note, Don Byas is at the Blue…

was over there, this was my thing. So I come in one night and changed the thing, come out fresh, put that old cologne on me. ("Hey,") Benny Bailey said, "Could I play one?" I said, "Yeah, man, come on." "Thank you, thank you."

Benny Bailey got up there and started playing "Star Dust" and we're running so much stuff, I said, look, stay right up there. "You stay right up there." See, I'm not going to get up there because that man was running too much stuff. He played the whole set. I said, ladies and gentlemen (inaudible) this is the man that's the greatest....beautiful.
